summary: Gives recommendations from the IETF IPv6 Working Group to the 3GPP mobile standards community on how to use IPv6. These include allowing multiple prefixes per primary PDP context and not assigning one prefix to more than one primary PDP context.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3314 recommends changes to how 3GPP mobile networks assign IPv6 address prefixes. The changes let a device use multiple prefixes and identifiers instead of limiting it to one address per connection.

subtitle: IPv6 addressing recommendations for the 3GPP mobile-network standards.

tldr.problem: The 3GPP IPv6 setup described in the RFC gave each primary PDP context one prefix and one interface identifier. That restricted the multiple addresses and identifiers expected by IPv6 hosts.
tldr.mechanism: The IPv6 Working Group recommended allowing multiple prefixes per primary PDP context, assigning each prefix to only one such context, and allowing multiple identifiers within those prefixes.
tldr.outcome: The RFC records recommendations, not a standard. Its text says 3GPP adopted the two primary recommendations in March 2002 and applied the changes to earlier releases.

facts.label: Recommended prefixes
facts.value: Multiple prefixes per primary PDP context

facts.label: Prefix assignment
facts.value: A prefix should belong to only one primary PDP context

today: RFC 3314 is an Informational recommendation document. It states that 3GPP adopted the two primary recommendations at its March 2002 plenary meeting and applied them to earlier releases.

sections.title: IPv6 Addressing in a PDP Context
sections.content:
A primary Packet Data Protocol (PDP) context connects user equipment to a gateway in the 3GPP packet network. The RFC explains that the 3GPP setup it reviews assigned one interface identifier and advertised one /64 prefix for that context, producing one IPv6 address.

IPv6 hosts can use multiple addresses on an interface and can form addresses from advertised prefixes and interface identifiers. Limiting a context to one assigned combination prevents use of those capabilities, including randomly generated identifiers described for privacy.
sections.plainLanguage: A PDP context is a connection between a mobile device and a network gateway. The setup described here gave that connection one IPv6 prefix and identifier, while an Internet-connected device can use more than one.

sections.title: Three Recommendations
sections.content:
The IPv6 Working Group recommends that 3GPP allow multiple prefixes to be advertised for each primary PDP context. It also recommends that a prefix not be assigned to more than one primary context, and that 3GPP nodes be allowed to use multiple identifiers within assigned prefixes, including randomly generated identifiers.

The RFC says these changes would let nodes use standard IPv6 address configuration and support multiple address types. It recommends that the Serving GPRS Support Node track prefixes associated with a context rather than depend on a single full IPv6 address to identify it.
sections.plainLanguage: Each main mobile connection may receive several address prefixes, but each prefix should belong to only one connection. Devices should also be allowed to form more than one address identifier within those prefixes.

sections.title: Why a /64 Prefix Is Considered Practical
sections.content:
The RFC considers whether assigning a /64 to each primary PDP context would use too much IPv6 address space. Using the Host Density Ratio assumptions described in the text, it estimates that 490 trillion /64 prefixes could be assigned from the address space it considers.

The document translates that estimate to around 80,000 PDP contexts per person and concludes that the space is sufficient even if non-3GPP networks use many prefixes. These are estimates made by the RFC from its stated assumptions, not protocol limits.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC estimates that IPv6 has enough space to assign a /64 prefix to each primary context. Its estimate depends on the address-allocation assumptions it describes.

sections.title: Implementation Options and Scope
sections.content:
The RFC considers ways to provide multiple addresses on a context. It recommends advertising one or more /64 prefixes through standard IPv6 Router Advertisements, allowing the device to form additional addresses. The GGSN can maintain prefixes for an Access Point Name and the SGSN can track the prefixes assigned to each context.

This document offers advice to the 3GPP community and defines no standard. It also lists further IPv6 work for the IETF, including guidance for IPv6 over PDP contexts. Its security section says the recommendations introduce no new security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The network can advertise prefixes and let the device use standard IPv6 rules to form addresses. This RFC gives recommendations and leaves any new protocol specification to other work.
